stem: A solutions architect must ensure every production change is deployed through a versioned pipeline rather than applied directly to a running instance. Which practice satisfies this?

choices.text: Provision infrastructure from templates, and make configuration fixes directly in the console for routine changes.
Apply patches directly to the running fleet on a recurring schedule.
Use an Auto Scaling group's health checks to terminate and relaunch any instance that fails a check.
Deploy every application change as a new machine image or template through the pipeline, replacing the running resource instead of modifying it in place.

rationale: Replacing a resource with a freshly built image or template each time a change is needed is immutable infrastructure: it makes every deployment atomic and leaves no running resource that was ever hand-edited, which is exactly what a versioned pipeline requires. Provisioning from templates but still allowing direct console fixes keeps one path where a resource is changed outside the pipeline, so the running fleet can still drift from what the template describes. Applying patches on a schedule directly to the running fleet changes resources in place rather than replacing them, which is the opposite of routing every change through the pipeline. Auto Scaling health checks only replace instances that fail a check; they do nothing to control how a deliberate application change is delivered, so they do not by themselves close the gap between the pipeline and the running fleet.
